strings.name: Yoshua Bengio
strings.role: Deep learning and representation learning · AI safety
strings.summary: Yoshua Bengio advanced neural networks, representation learning and neural language models while training researchers at Université de Montréal and building the Mila research community. He shared the Turing Award with Geoffrey Hinton and Yann LeCun and coauthored a major deep-learning textbook. More recently he has focused on AI risks and safety through the nonprofit LawZero; its proposed safeguards remain subjects of theoretical and empirical investigation.
strings.coverageNote: Research checked through 13 November 2026; selected milestones extend to 2026. This is not a daily news record. Shared achievements are credited to collaborators and teams.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced deep-learning theory, representation learning and Canada’s AI research community, while contributing to AI safety and governance debates.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Representations and language models
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Researched distributed word representations and neural language models with collaborators, and coauthored Deep Learning.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Research community and safety
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Trained machine-learning researchers, developed Mila and explored safer AI designs through LawZero.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Scientist AI safety argument
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Led a team presenting a formal safety framework whose conclusions depend on assumptions, not an absolute guarantee.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Launched LawZero
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Announced a nonprofit AI research organization exploring safer systems centered on prediction and understanding.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: 2018 Turing Award announced
strings.timeline.event-3.text: ACM named him a joint recipient with Geoffrey Hinton and Yann LeCun for deep learning.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Coauthored Deep Learning
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Published the textbook with Ian Goodfellow and Aaron Courville.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Neural language-model paper
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Studied word representations and probabilistic language modeling with Réjean Ducharme, Pascal Vincent and Christian Jauvin.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Joined Université de Montréal
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Began teaching computer science and operations research and gradually built a machine-learning research group.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Computer science doctorate
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Completed his McGill PhD before postdoctoral research at MIT and Bell Labs.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Engineering degree
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Graduated from McGill before pursuing graduate study in computer science.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Born in Paris
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Born in Paris, France; later studied and built his research career in Canada.
